article.title: Revenue Growth Can Hide Customer Concentration Risk
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A company can report strong revenue growth and still become more fragile. One reason is customer concentration: a growing share of sales may come from a small number of large customers. At first, this can look attractive. Winning a major account can lift revenue quickly, improve sales efficiency, and create a strong reference for future customers. But the same success can increase dependence.

Suppose a software company grows revenue from $100 million to $130 million. That 30 percent increase sounds excellent. Now suppose one customer accounts for $25 million of the new total. If that customer reduces spending, delays renewal, or negotiates a large discount, the impact can be much larger than the headline growth rate suggests. The important question is therefore not only how fast revenue is growing, but also where the growth comes from.

Customer concentration creates several types of risk. The first is renewal risk. A large contract can create a visible drop in revenue if it is not renewed. The second is bargaining power. A customer that represents a large share of sales may know that the supplier cannot easily afford to lose the relationship. It may ask for lower prices, special product features, longer payment terms, or additional support. The third is operational concentration. Teams may spend so much time serving one large account that the product gradually becomes less useful for the broader market.

Concentration is not automatically bad. Some businesses naturally begin with a few anchor customers, and a large client can provide stable demand for years. The issue is whether management understands the dependency and has a credible plan to manage it. Analysts can examine the percentage of revenue from the top one, top five, or top ten customers. They can also compare contract lengths, renewal dates, customer industries, and geographic exposure.

Trend matters more than one isolated number. If the top customer represents 12 percent of revenue this year versus 5 percent two years ago, concentration is rising even if total revenue is growing. Conversely, a company can reduce risk by adding new customers faster than its largest accounts grow. This is why customer count alone is not enough: ten tiny customers do not offset one enormous contract.

Managers should connect concentration metrics to scenarios. What happens to revenue, gross profit, cash flow, and staffing if the largest customer cuts spending by 20 percent? How quickly could the lost volume be replaced? Are sales incentives encouraging teams to chase a few giant deals while ignoring a diversified pipeline? These questions turn a static concentration ratio into a business decision.

Healthy growth therefore has two dimensions: scale and resilience. Revenue growth tells us that the company is selling more. Customer concentration tells us how dependent that growth may be on a small set of relationships. Looking at both prevents a strong headline number from hiding a weaker underlying structure.
paragraphs.zh: 公司即使營收高速成長，也可能因客戶集中度上升而變得更脆弱。大型客戶能快速推升收入，但也增加續約、議價與營運集中風險。分析時不只看 revenue growth，也要看 top 1、top 5、top 10 客戶占比、合約期限、續約時間與產業分布。單一年度的集中度不如趨勢重要；若最大客戶占比從 5% 升到 12%，即使總營收增加，依賴仍在加深。管理者還應做情境分析，例如最大客戶削減 20% 支出時，收入、毛利、現金流與人力會受到什麼影響。健康成長同時包含規模與韌性。
paragraphs.ja: 売上高が大きく成長していても、顧客集中度が高まれば企業は脆弱になる可能性があります。大口顧客は短期間で売上を伸ばしますが、更新、価格交渉、業務集中のリスクも高めます。分析ではrevenue growthだけでなく、上位1社・5社・10社の売上比率、契約期間、更新時期、業界分布を確認します。単年度の比率よりトレンドが重要で、最大顧客比率が5%から12%へ上がれば、総売上が伸びても依存度は増しています。最大顧客が支出を20%減らした場合の売上、粗利、cash flow、人員への影響をscenarioで見ることも重要です。健全な成長には規模とresilienceの両方が必要です。

vocabulary.usage: Customer concentration can rise during growth.
The business may become more fragile.
A large contract creates renewal risk.
Large customers may gain bargaining power.

phrases.example: One customer accounts for 20 percent of sales.
Check the underlying structure of growth.

grammar.title: not only A, but also B
grammar.body: 用來強調分析不能只看 A，也要看 B。

business.term: Where is the growth coming from?
business.example: Before celebrating the headline, where is the growth coming from?
What is our largest-customer exposure after renewal?

quiz.question: Why can customer concentration make growth risky?
quiz.answer: Because losing or repricing a large customer can have an outsized impact.
